steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: A stimulus can be anything: an image, a song, a news story, a poem, an object — it's the starting point for devising. | Key Fact: Research: explore the stimulus from multiple angles — personal, social, historical, political — to find depth. | Key Fact: Brainstorming: generate as many ideas as possible without judging them — quantity leads to quality. | Key Fact: Collaborative creation: everyone contributes — share ideas physically and verbally, build on each other's suggestions.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe the process you would use to develop a piece of drama from a stimulus. Use a specific example. | How can research enhance a devised piece? What types of research might you do? | Explain how collaborative devising is different from working with a script. What are the challenges and benefits?
